 House Democrats Oppose USDA Effort to Take Food Assistance Away from Millions of Americans
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on X 
 Print this Page 
 Share by Email 
 Washington, 
 November 19, 2026 
 | 
 Britton T. Burdick 
 Tags: 
 Nutrition and Foreign Agriculture 
 , 
 Full Committee 
 Today, House Agriculture Committee  Ranking Member Angie Craig (MN-02)  led 213 members of the House Democratic Caucus in a letter to U.S. Department of Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins opposing a  new proposed rule  that would kick an estimated 6.3 million Americans – primarily older or disabled recipeints and families with children – off the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). Experts have argued that  the rule is illegal  and that only Congress has the authority to change broad-based categorical eligiblity (BBCE).
 The proposed rule would undercut BBCE, an optional mechanism used by U.S. states and territories to improve efficiency and reduce administrative burdens by granting SNAP eligibility to Americans in need if they already qualify for similar means-tested programs.
 “BBCE has been used by red and blue states alike for nearly 30 years to reduce administrative red tape, ease SNAP’s benefit cliff, and allow families to save for their future,”  write the lawmakers .
 They continue , “According to the Department’s own regulatory impact analysis of the proposed rule, 6.3 million individuals in 3.2 million households will lose their SNAP benefits entirely.”
 “This proposed rule comes a little over a year after the largest cut to SNAP in history, with 5.5 million people having lost food assistance due to the changes advocated for by this administration,”  the letter writers note .
 The Democratic lawmakers conclude,  “This rule will increase hunger, cost states more, exacerbate the affordability crisis for millions and make passing a farm bill more complicated.”
 Read the letter here .
 Under President Trump and Secretary Rollins, food insecurity in America has increased, according to  independent analysis .  Food inflation accelerated  in October.  Thanksgiving staples are up 11 percent  year-over-year.
